_game: SuperTuxKart (sports/racing) -- the current game, via the stk-code fork's gym server
_note: pip install 'fmri-gym[stk_gym]' (or supertuxkart-gym): the wheel fetches the game and a 254 MiB asset pack from its GitHub release on first use, Linux x86_64 only. To work on the engine, build the fork instead (see README); a checkout is preferred over the download, and STK_ENV_BIN overrides both. Needs a real OpenGL display: the game renders into a hidden window and every frame is read back and shown here; it does not work under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy or with --render-driver=vulkan.
_keys_note: The env's action is MultiBinary(8) over SuperTuxKart's keys, so 'keys' values are indices: 0=left, 1=right, 2=up (accelerate), 3=down (brake / reverse), 4=nitro, 5=skid, 6=fire, 7=rescue; held keys combine and the game's own player controller turns them into controls. The map below is SuperTuxKart's default bindings; keep the Controls text in sync by hand.
_timing_note: The game is lock-stepped: one step per frame, frame_skip physics ticks (120 Hz) per step, so fps must equal 120 / frame_skip; the adapter refuses otherwise. Measured 2.5 ms per step at 640x360 with four karts on an Intel Arc laptop.
_logging_note: Per frame: actions (the 8-vector), reward (progress, metres), and every SAMPLE_FIELDS column from stk_gym: tick/time/phase, speed, x/y/z, heading, distance_down_track, distance_to_center, on_road/on_ground/wrong_way, rank, finished_laps, powerup, nitro_energy, progress_m, ctrl_* (the controls the kart applied). Frames are shown, not stored. A block replays from episode_seeds + actions with the same track, karts, seed and binary: python ../stk-code/python/examples/replay_log.py <block.npz>.
